profile_text.body:
Microsoft is a public company traded as MSFT, with CIK 0000789019, founded in 1975 and headquartered in Redmond, Washington. The page harvested from its site covers Power Automate, which the company describes as a way to automate workflows and business processes across apps, systems, and websites using AI, digital, and robotic process automation. The same page presents customer accounts of using generative AI and Power Automate together, including one customer stating that a data validation and standardization process that once took over 100 people can now be managed by a few.

Its AI products span several areas. Microsoft Copilot is embedded across M365, and Azure OpenAI Service offers OpenAI models in Azure regions with enterprise content filtering, Entra ID integration, and data residency controls. Azure Machine Learning provides an MLOps platform with AutoML, a model registry, and responsible AI toolkit integration. Power Automate AI covers enterprise workflow automation with Copilot integration, M365 data access, and DLP integration, while Teams AI, SharePoint AI, and Clipchamp AI apply AI to meetings, enterprise content, and video editing. Developer tools include AutoGen, a multi-agent conversation framework from Microsoft Research, Semantic Kernel, a model-agnostic orchestration SDK for .NET, Python, and Java, and Microsoft Agent Framework, described as the successor to Semantic Kernel and AutoGen with graph workflows and native MCP and A2A support. Microsoft Designer covers image and design generation.

The company's most recent 10-K, for the period ending 2026-06-30, reports revenue of $331,839,000,000. Litigation involving the company includes The New York Times Co. v. Microsoft Corp. and OpenAI and Authors Guild v. OpenAI, Inc., both in the U.S. District Court, S.D. New York. Its litigation exposure includes 114 cases in Washington.
